reviewed: borsapy 0.10.1, installed source, read-only inspection on 2026-10-06; no borsapy calls and no network requests
method: Two readers (fund.py with _providers/tefas.py; the rest of the package) and one reviewer asked to refute: 'only unit price is dated fund history'. Paths are relative to site-packages.

fund_api.history_beyond_price:
No. Within fund.py, the classes it inherits from and every provider they call, unit price is the only dated time series. Fund.history() reads just tarih and fiyat from each fonFiyatBilgiGetir row (tefas.py:525-551). Everything else is undated or a placeholder:

- **Fund size / AUM:** history() sets FundSize=float('nan') on every row (tefas.py:553). The only real value is info['fund_size'] (portBuyukluk, tefas.py:355), and info['date'] is hardcoded '' (tefas.py:353).
- **Investor count:** history() sets Investors=0 on every row (tefas.py:554). info['investor_count'] (yatirimciSayi, tefas.py:356) is a snapshot.
- **Units outstanding:** not exposed anywhere. A grep finds no payAdet in tefas.py.
- **Allocation:** only the current page snapshot, loaded through a stealth browser and stamped Date=datetime.now() (tefas.py:658, 673). allocation_history() deletes period, start and end and returns that same snapshot (fund.py:327-330), and get_allocation() discards start, end and fund_type (tefas.py:640-641). The old allocation-history path is dead code: ASSET_TYPE_MAPPING, commented 'Used by BindHistoryAllocation API' (tefas.py:21-74), and the legacy /api/DB helper _post_json (tefas.py:195-225) are never referenced in the package.
- **Holdings:** get_holdings() returns one KAP report per call: the latest, or a YYYY-MM within a hard-coded 365-day lookback, otherwise silently the latest (kap_holdings.py:438, 446-458). The DataFrame has no date column (kap_holdings.py:523-533). report_date is computed (kap_holdings.py:482-491) but only kept in a private cache (kap_holdings.py:494). Parsing needs a paid OpenRouter LLM (kap_holdings.py:263-293).
- **Category membership:** info category, category_rank and category_fund_count are current only (tefas.py:363, 381-382). screen_funds and search_funds list only today's funds, with no dates (tefas.py:776-834, 981-996).
- **Fees:** management_fee and management_fees (fonYonetimBazliBilgiGetir, tefas.py:1023-1044) and info entry_fee/exit_fee (tefas.py:394-395) carry no effective date.
- **Returns and risk:** return_1m to return_5y (tefas.py:370-376) and risk_value (tefas.py:364-368) are undated snapshots.

The only dated non-price items in scope:
- The KAP disclosure list behind get_holdings: publish_date, year and month per monthly portfolio report (kap_holdings.py:143-154). It is a private provider method and returns report metadata, not holdings values.
- The static withholding-tax schedule's legal period boundaries (tax.py:27-46). This is reference data, not fund history.

Technical-indicator series are dated only because they are computed from the price series.

other_modules.history_beyond_price:
No. Nothing in scope returns dated history for fund size/AUM, investor count, units outstanding, allocation, holdings, category membership or fees. All paths below are relative to borsapy/.

(1) Holdings and allocation: the only dated source is metadata. KAPHoldingsProvider.get_disclosures (_providers/kap_holdings.py:116-159) returns, for the "Portföy Dağılım Raporu" type only (L22, L135):
- publish_date: raw "DD.MM.YYYY HH:MM:SS" string, unparsed (L148)
- year (L151)
- period = donem month (L152)
It covers a rolling `days` window (default 365, L119). The module is private and unexported (__init__.py:214-338; _providers/__init__.py exports only BaseProvider), and Fund never calls it.

The contents path, get_holdings/get_holdings_df (L396-537), is what Fund.get_holdings uses (fund.py:571-574). It needs a paid OpenRouter LLM and extra packages (L225-293, L236-251), and it drops the date: report_date is computed at L481-491 but kept only in the private cache (L494). Neither Holding (L31-42) nor the DataFrame columns (L514-533) have a date. A requested period missing from the 365-day list silently returns the latest report (L438, L446-458).

Allocation is only displayed by the CLI from fund.py (cli/commands/fund.py:207-231). portfolio.py's "allocation" and "holdings" are the user's own positions and target weights (portfolio.py:61-69, 301-336, 526-585), not fund holdings.

(2) AUM and investors: only Fund.info's undated latest values are displayed, defaulting to 0 (cli/commands/fund.py:112, 338-339). Their source sets info["date"] = "" (tefas.py:353-356). The aum_usd in tradingview_etf.py:265 belongs to foreign ETFs holding a BIST stock, has no date field, and is not TEFAS data.

(3) Units outstanding: no reference in any in-scope file. A grep for payAdet, units, tedavül and shares_outstanding found nothing.

(4) Category membership: tax.withholding_tax_rate uses today's info["category"] for any historical purchase date (tax.py:278-283). The rest of tax.py is a static table (L27-46, L76-145). There is no dated membership anywhere.

(5) Fees: none in scope. management_fees lives in fund.py (exported at __init__.py:160). expense_ratio in tradingview_etf.py:264 is a foreign-ETF snapshot with no date.

(6) KAP stock paths cannot fill these gaps. KAPProvider resolves only BIST stock codes (kap.py:193-215), its calendar asks only for memberTypes IGS (kap.py:311), and the portfolio report is the only disclosure-type ID in the package.

(7) EVDS (_providers/evds.py:1-43) is a generic, dated TCMB series client with no fund-specific code. Whether its catalog carries fund-sector aggregates cannot be determined from source.

capabilities.upstream: KAP GET https://kap.org.tr/tr/api/disclosure/filter/FILTERYFBF/{fundId}/8aca490d502e34b801502e380044002b/{days} (L59, L135). fundId comes from get_fund_id (L70-114): TEFAS get_fund_detail()['kap_link'] (L90-95; tefas.py:396 maps it from fonProfilBilgiGetir kapLink), then a GET of that KAP fund page and the regex objId (L100-109).
capabilities.returns: list[dict] with disclosure_id, disclosure_index, publish_date, title, summary, year, period (= KAP donem, the month number), attachment_count (L145-154). get_latest_disclosure returns disclosures[0].
dated_fields: publish_date (raw KAP publishDate string 'DD.MM.YYYY HH:MM:SS', unparsed, no UTC offset; L148)
placeholder_fields: attachment_count defaults to 0 if absent (L153)
capabilities.requires: None: public KAP and TEFAS endpoints. Private module: not exported (__init__.py:214-338) and never called by Fund (fund.py:571-574 calls only get_holdings_df).
capabilities.notes:
The only dated, fund-specific KAP capability in the package, and it returns metadata only (the report itself is a PDF attachment).

Coverage limits:
- Only one disclosure type is wired. The 32-hex ID at L22 is the sole disclosure-type ID in the whole package, so there are no material events, prospectus (izahname) changes or other fund filings.
- The window is a rolling `days` value.
- Order is assumed newest-first and never sorted (L164-165).
- KAP fields isChanged, isLate, relatedDisclosureIndex and disclosureClass are dropped, so amendments can't be detected. They were null or false in the spike's 25 raw records.

Error handling:
- get_fund_id turns every exception into None (L113-114), and get_disclosures then raises 'Fund not found in KAP' (L132-133). Network, redirect and parse failures therefore look the same as a missing fund.
- The shared httpx client sets no follow_redirects (base.py:33-35) but does verify TLS (base.py:23, 34), unlike the TEFAS provider.

Local evidence (spike raw files, not re-run): year and donem are JSON integers; publishDate looks like '05.10.2026 13:00:53'; TTE had 13 records, newest-first. spike.py:323 uses the identical objId regex, and each of the TTE and AAL pages had exactly one objId.

counter_evidence.finding: KAPHoldingsProvider.get_disclosures(fund_code, days=365) returns a dated list, for one fund, of its KAP 'Portföy Dağılım Raporu' filings: publish_date, year, period (the report month), title, summary, disclosure_index and attachment_count (L143-154). The days lookback goes into the KAP request URL (L135). I checked the spike's saved responses offline: year and donem are ints, and the 365-day window held 13 monthly reports for TTE (2025-09 to 2026-09) and 12 for AAL.
counter_evidence.admissible: Needs no API key, LLM or browser. It is in a private module: borsapy._providers.kap_holdings is not exported by borsapy/__init__.py or _providers/__init__.py (which exports only BaseProvider), and Fund only calls it internally through get_holdings (kap_holdings.py:438). It gives filing metadata (filing time and report month), not fund values. publish_date is an unparsed 'DD.MM.YYYY HH:MM:SS' string with no offset. It needs TEFAS's kapLink plus a regex scrape of the KAP page for objId (L93-109), and any failure there turns into None and then DataNotAvailableError (L113-114, L131-133). Whether KAP honors days>365 can't be determined from source. KAP terms not reviewed.

counter_evidence.finding: The public Fund.get_holdings(api_key, period='YYYY-MM') picks a past month's portfolio report by year and month (kap_holdings.py:446-456) from the last-365-day disclosure list (kap_holdings.py:438), downloads its PDF and returns that month's holdings (symbol, name, weight, market value). So KAP holdings can be fetched for past months, not only the latest one.
counter_evidence.admissible: The output carries no date. report_date is computed (kap_holdings.py:481-491) but only kept in a private cache tuple (L494), and the DataFrame has no date column (L523-533). If the requested month is missing, it silently returns the latest report instead (L457-458), so the output can't confirm which month you got. It requires an OpenRouter key plus pymupdf4llm and openai (L236-251), and sends up to 80,000 characters of PDF text to a third-party LLM, by default google/gemini-3-flash-preview (L28, L258-266, L290-293). Cost can't be determined from source; the docstring says 'free API key' (fund.py:537). The prompt asks only for stock rows and never asks for ISIN (L269-284), so isin and country are usually None and non-equity holdings are dropped. LLM output can vary between runs.

counter_evidence.finding: _get_file_id(disclosure_index) (L168-192) and _download_pdf(file_id) (L194-223) fetch the raw monthly portfolio-report PDF for any disclosure returned by get_disclosures, with no LLM and no key. Each PDF is dated by its disclosure's year, month and publish_date.
counter_evidence.admissible: Private underscore methods. The content is a PDF, so you need your own parser. Errors are swallowed and returned as None (L191-192, L222-223). KAP terms not reviewed.

counter_evidence.finding: Ticker(symbol).history() (ticker.py:676-746) asks TradingView for f'BIST:{symbol}' without checking that the symbol is a stock (tradingview.py:397-399). It returns dated OHLCV plus Volume and honors start/end (L519-536). bp.search(type='fund' or 'etf') maps to TradingView's 'fund' type (tradingview_search.py:37-38; search.py:45). For exchange-traded funds listed on BIST, this gives dated history beyond a single price: open, high, low, close and volume.
counter_evidence.admissible: This is a different universe: exchange-traded fund shares on BIST, not TEFAS mutual funds, and it gives market price and volume, not NAV, size or investor count. It uses an unofficial TradingView websocket with 'unauthorized_user_token' when not logged in (tradingview.py:304-309). Which codes resolve can't be determined from source, and a TEFAS code that matches a BIST symbol would silently return that other instrument. TradingView terms not reviewed.

counter_evidence.finding: Fund inherits TwitterMixin (fund.py:15). Its query is built at fund.py:54-60 and twitter.py:81-100. Fund.tweets(since, until) passes the date window to Scweet (L187-189, L209-215) and returns a created_at timestamp for each tweet (L288, L314), giving dated historical posts that mention the fund.
counter_evidence.admissible: Not admissible. It requires logged-in X session cookies (auth_token and ct0) (L19-60, L128-133) and the optional Scweet package, and it scrapes. The result is social chatter, not fund data, and a bare short fund code in the query (twitter.py:92) makes it noisy.

nuances: The practical core of the claim holds: for TEFAS numeric fields, borsapy has no dated history besides price. get_history keeps only tarih and fiyat and hard-codes FundSize=NaN and Investors=0 (_providers/tefas.py:538-556). get_fund_detail hard-codes date='' (tefas.py:353), even though Fund.info documents it as 'Last update date' (fund.py:114). Fund size, investor count, category, rank, market share, 1m-5y returns, entry and exit fees and profile come back as latest values only (tefas.py:350-401). screen_funds, compare_funds, search and management_fees are undated too (tefas.py:739-1049). I checked the spike's saved raw responses offline: fonBilgiGetir, fonProfilBilgiGetir and fonGetiriBazliBilgiGetir contain no date field, so borsapy isn't dropping a source date.

Units outstanding aren't a 'latest-only' field in borsapy. They aren't exposed at all: payAdet is never read (it's absent from tefas.py:350-401), even though TEFAS's fonBilgiGetir returns it (spike raw/fonBilgiGetir_TTE.body).

KAP disclosure metadata is dated and needs no key or LLM (kap_holdings.py:116-159). It's reachable only by importing the private borsapy._providers.kap_holdings module, and it gives filing dates and report months, not values.

'KAP holdings need a paid LLM' is imprecise. Only borsapy's built-in parser uses the LLM; the raw PDFs can be fetched without it (kap_holdings.py:168-223). The source doesn't establish any cost: fund.py:537 says 'free API key', and the model is set at kap_holdings.py:28. The real constraints are sending PDF text to a third-party model, output that can vary between runs, and a prompt that asks only for stocks (L269-284).

KAP holdings aren't latest-only. Fund.get_holdings(period='YYYY-MM') can reach about the last 12 monthly reports, because the disclosure list covers 365 days (kap_holdings.py:438). The output has no date, though, and silently falls back to the latest report when the month isn't found (L457-458).
KAP gives monthly data with a lag. The spike saw reports published about 3-10 days after month end. The month a report covers comes from year/donem, not from a holdings as-of date.

Allocation 'stamped with today' means the fetch time, datetime.now() (tefas.py:658, 673), not TEFAS's as-of date. start and end are deleted (tefas.py:641), and allocation_history ignores period, start and end (fund.py:295-330). Rows are deduplicated by asset type, keeping the first match (tefas.py:659-664). Whether the SSR page carries its own date can't be determined from source.

No historical allocation path remains. BindHistoryAllocation appears only in a comment (tefas.py:21). The legacy /api/DB helper _post_json is defined (tefas.py:195-225) but nothing calls it, and the docstring says allocation is no longer in any JSON endpoint (tefas.py:606-608). Whether the legacy endpoints still respond can't be determined from source. The private _post_json_v2 can call any TEFAS v2 endpoint (tefas.py:227-287), but that's code you'd write yourself, not a borsapy feature.

Every fonFiyatBilgiGetir row also contains kategoriDerece and kategoriFonSay (spike raw row keys: fiyat, fonKodu, fonUnvan, kategoriDerece, kategoriFonSay, tarih). borsapy drops them (tefas.py:540-541), which is correct: the spike found them constant across all rows.

Derived outputs are dated but add nothing beyond price. technicals() and history_with_indicators() use the price history (technical.py:1065-1095). risk_metrics() and sharpe_ratio() are computed from it (fund.py:386-519), and Portfolio.history uses the Price column (portfolio.py:678-680). Scalar helpers such as rsi() drop the date (technical.py:1097-1117). Fund doesn't implement _get_ta_symbol_info, so TradingView TA signals aren't available for funds (technical.py:1405-1421).

Snapshot values can be dated by inference, not from the API. The spike found that sonFiyat equals the newest history price and that gunlukGetiri matches the last two prices. That is the as-of rule in REPORT.md.

You can build your own history by saving snapshots every day, but borsapy stores nothing. Its cache is in-memory with a time limit only (cache.py:19-62). TTL.FUND_DATA is defined but never used (cache.py:75). There is no sqlite, pickle or file writer; the CLI formatter only writes CSV to stdout. replay, backtest and multi accept only Ticker (replay.py:450-454; backtest.py:564; multi.py:42).

history() window quirks: a start date older than about 5 years is silently cut to 5 years (tefas.py:467-478). An unknown period returns 1 month (tefas.py:482). '2y' fetches 3 years (tefas.py:123). '1d' and '5d' fetch the weekly bucket (tefas.py:114-115).

EVDS provides generic dated series that honor start and end (evds.py:64-85, 285-329, 647-723) and needs a free registered key (_providers/evds.py:907-913). The borsapy source names no fund-related series: neither evds.py nor _providers/evds.py contains fon, fund, menkul, portföy or yatırım. Whether TCMB publishes fund statistics there can't be determined from source, and they would be aggregates at best, not per fund.

tax.py ships a dated withholding-tax rate schedule (TAX_PERIODS and TAX_RATES, tax.py:27-46), used by Fund.withholding_tax_rate(purchase_date) (fund.py:229-265). It's static regulatory data applied using today's category, not fund observations.

The stock KAPProvider can't list fund disclosures. Its codes come only from the BIST companies page (kap.py:191-218), and an unknown code returns an empty frame (kap.py:237-239). Its get_disclosure_content(disclosure_id) works for any code (kap.py:505-522). There's no path to fund material events or prospectus changes: the only disclosure-type ID in the package is the portfolio report (kap_holdings.py:22).
Ticker.etf_holders returns an undated snapshot of international ETFs that hold a stock, including their AUM (tradingview_etf.py:46-67, 256-267). It isn't TEFAS data and carries no date.
refutation_check.summary:
The claim is refuted, but only narrowly. The practical core holds.

**What holds.** For TEFAS fund fields, borsapy 0.10.1 gives dated history only for the unit price.
- `get_history` keeps only `tarih` and `fiyat`, and fills FundSize and Investors with NaN and 0 (_providers/tefas.py:538-556).
- `get_fund_detail` hard-codes `date=''` (tefas.py:353). Fund size, investors, category, rank, market share, returns, fees and profile come back as undated latest values (tefas.py:350-401).
- Units outstanding (`payAdet`) are not exposed at all, so they aren't even a latest value.
- Allocation is stamped with `datetime.now()`, and its start/end arguments are thrown away (tefas.py:641, 658).
- The old dated endpoints (BindHistoryAllocation, /api/DB) survive only as a comment and a helper nothing calls (tefas.py:21, 195-225).
- Nothing is stored: the cache is in memory only (cache.py:19-62).

**Why the headline is still false.** "The only dated historical fund data is the unit price" fails because of KAP:
1. `KAPHoldingsProvider.get_disclosures` (_providers/kap_holdings.py:116-159) returns a dated list of one fund's monthly portfolio-report filings: publishDate, year and report month. The lookback is passed to KAP, and it needs no key or LLM. It lives in a private module that borsapy doesn't export, and it gives filing metadata, not fund values.
2. The public `Fund.get_holdings(api_key, period='YYYY-MM')` (fund.py:521; kap_holdings.py:438-458) returns holdings for past months within a 365-day window, so KAP holdings are not latest-only. But:
   - the output has no date column;
   - it silently falls back to the latest report when the month isn't found;
   - it depends on a third-party LLM whose cost the source doesn't establish (the docstring says "free API key").
   - The raw dated PDFs can be fetched without the LLM through `_get_file_id` and `_download_pdf` (kap_holdings.py:168-223).

**Other dated paths, outside TEFAS mutual funds:**
- `Ticker()` on exchange-traded funds listed on BIST gives dated OHLCV and volume through TradingView (tradingview.py:397-536).
- `Fund.tweets(since, until)` gives dated tweets, but needs logged-in X session cookies.
- Neither is admissible fund data here.
- EVDS offers generic dated series, but the source names no fund series.

**Answer to the user.** No, borsapy isn't limited to the fund's price. It can read many fund fields, but as dated history it gives only:
- the unit price from TEFAS (5-year maximum);
- monthly KAP portfolio-report filings, as dates, raw PDFs or LLM-parsed holdings.

Size, investors, units, category, rank, returns, fees, profile and allocation have no history unless you save the snapshot yourself every day.

**Method.** This was read-only. I read the installed source and the spike's saved raw files (to confirm year and month are integers, so `get_holdings` can match a requested month). No network calls or borsapy calls. The tefas.py and fund.py hashes match REPORT.md.

**Not done.** I did not commit, push or open the PR on spike/tefas-and-helpers that the user approved. That was outside this read-only task and still needs to be run.
